description: Spec Section 2. Five conversion logic laws. One is selected per post.

contrapositive.name: Contrapositive / Cost-of-Inaction
narrative_template: Name the desired result the customer wants.
Name what is preventing that result today.
Show the honest ongoing cost of that gap (inconvenience, delay, uncertainty).
Show how the product legitimately reduces that gap.
Close with what changes.
guardrails: No catastrophic outcomes unsupported by the product.
contrapositive.example: If you're still planning your day around the nearest outlet, your backup power isn't giving you enough freedom.

disjunctive.name: Disjunctive Inference / Decision Simplification
narrative_template: Name the current alternative the customer uses today.
Name what becomes possible with the product.
Show the honest comparison (not a false dichotomy).
Close with the simplified decision.
guardrails: Use legitimate categories: manual vs automated, dependent vs portable, multiple tools vs consolidated.
disjunctive.example: You can keep carrying multiple charging solutions or consolidate your backup power into one portable setup.

double_implication.name: Double Implication / Promise-Delivery Alignment
narrative_template: State the promise clearly.
Name the specific feature or mechanism that supports it.
Show verifiable evidence.
Close with the meaning to the customer.
guardrails: Every major claim must have an underlying feature/spec/evidence.
Rewrite the claim if evidence does not support it.
Never invent statistics, savings, certifications, or reviews.
double_implication.example: Fast power when time matters — backed by 20W USB-C PD.

symmetrical_equivalence.name: Symmetrical Equivalence / Multiple Value Paths
symmetrical_equivalence.formal: p + q = R and q + p = R
narrative_template: Pick one specific feature/attribute as the entry point.
Trace it to the same central value proposition.
Signal that this is one of several paths to the same outcome.
Close on the shared outcome.
guardrails: Every entry point must legitimately connect to the same outcome.
Use to create creative diversity, not to rebrand the same claim.
symmetrical_equivalence.example: Capacity gets you through the day. Speed gets you back on the road. Either way: dependable portable power.

result_traceability.name: Result Traceability / Feature-to-Outcome Chain
narrative_template: Name the feature or spec.
Explain the mechanism (why it works).
State the benefit in customer terms.
Show the outcome in a real situation.
Anchor with verifiable evidence.
guardrails: Every step must be legitimately supported by product data.
result_traceability.example: 20,000mAh -> stores backup energy -> extended portable charging -> more time away from outlets -> verified product spec.
